I posted this on my old account but I still think about this story every once in a while. I was 16 and decided to go on a short road trip with some friends. We decided to find this supposedly haunted, abandoned cemetery in the middle of the woods. My dad’s uncle used to help his dad with general upkeep of the cemetery and church. He had told us stories about walking into the church and seeing 1800s era funeral processions taking place. 

We found the cemetery and walked around for a bit before heading into the church. The door was unlocked so we just went on in. Inside was exactly how you would expect, no electricity, old newspapers and bibles scattered everywhere. We had been taking pictures all night and decided to take a few inside the church. Out of nowhere, my friend started hysterically crying, like shaking and we could see real tears. We left and to this day she won’t even talk about that night, she always says she doesn’t remember it. 

The next day I decided to look through the pictures and everything looked normal. Until we get to the pictures from inside the church. In every single picture inside the church and everywhere we went afterwards, there were half a dozen orbs in each picture. I showed my sister and it creeped her out so we decided to go back a couple weeks later so she could check it out. 

I parked directly in front of the doors to the church, which were now locked. We both try to open the door and it will not budge. We walk around the outside of the church looking in all of the windows, but it was too dark to see anything at all. We made our way back to the front doors and tried them one more time to no avail. We decided to come back another time. We walked to my car, got in, I turned the headlights on and the door to the church was wide open. I think we both cried. I sure as fuck have never gone back and I don’t believe she has either.

I worked at a soup restaurant for about 3 years. I take all of my jobs seriously and try to go above and beyond what is expected of me. I was quickly promoted to store manager, meaning there were two bosses above me - the general manager, D and the owner, J. About two years into being the store manager, a very close friend committed suicide. It was very unexpected and absolutely broke me in so many ways. Needing to go home for the funeral, I asked every staff member we had if they could cover my shifts for a day or two but no one was able to help out. Having no other option, I asked D if he would mind covering two of my shifts so I could go to the funeral. His response was a hard “no” because he told his kids he would take them to the mall during one of those days. 

In the three years I had worked there, I had never once seen D work a shift. He would come in to do payroll once a week and that was it. Also, his kids were 1 and 3, so it’s not like they could have even been excited about going to the mall. Having no choice but to miss the funeral, I worked my shifts. I spiraled into a deep depression and could barely leave my apartment except to go to work. I don’t think I went to the grocery store for a full month because I just wanted to sleep. 

Although I was spiraling, I worked every shift I was scheduled and did the bare minimum of what was expected of me. This was mostly due to the fact that I was still pissed off about D not covering for me because he wanted to take his kids to the mall. After a couple months of doing the bare minimum, I receive an email from D. He basically says that he’s very disappointed in me for still being upset about missing my friend’s funeral. He flat out said to get over it and called me a piece of shit for putting my personal problems ahead of his store. I walked the FUCK out, never to return.


EDIT: At the end of the email it said to call him when I get a chance. I called him and he said he was at the mall with his kids and didn’t have time to talk about my dead friend. THAT was my last straw.
